messages.content: Can you use the 'update_user_info' function to update the name and email of a customer with user ID 12345 in the 'CustomerInfo' database to "John" and "example@.com", then repeat the same process for another customer with user ID 67890, changing their name and email to the same value as well as well?

function.name: update_user_info
function.description: Update user information in the database. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The user ID of the customer.

database.description: The database where the user's information is stored.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to call the function twice:

1) For user_id=12345, set name="John", email="example@.com".
2) For user_id=67890, also set name="John", email="example@.com".

We need to produce calls using the tool.

But we should check if there's anything about constraints or errors. There's no mention of restrictions on email format; but example has "example@.com". It's weird but okay.

Also note that they want to do it "and well"? They wrote "...changing their name and email to the same value as well as well?" That seems redundant. But basically both customers get same values.

Thus two separate calls.

We'll output JSON calls via the tool invocation. According to guidelines, each function call should be separate messages. We can combine them into one block? Usually it's recommended to make separate calls. We'll provide first call, then second call.

Let's craft the calls accordingly.

First call:
{
"user_id": 12345,
"update_info": {"name":"John","email":"example@.com"},
"database":"CustomerInfo"
}

Second call similar with user_id 67890.

Return nothing else. Just the calls.
